repositories.title: Yarn Spinner core

source.cache_limit: Pinned shallow default-head objects and selected blobs; not complete history or all branches.

evidence.lines: not used for a claim; core API implementation not required for pattern review

repositories.observed: README describes screenplay-like interactive dialogue that emits lines, options and commands to a larger game. The spec deliberately delegates presentation, option selection, generic command effects and function handling to that host (Yarn-Spec 42-49); generic commands communicate directions but the implementing program must not alter Yarn flow based on them (304-337). The repository README identifies this checkout as compiler core and points game integration to engine-specific packages; the official supported package listed here is Unity.
repositories.notice_and_purpose: MIT, preserve copyright/permission notice in copies or substantial portions. It is a C# compiler/core and dialogue language, not a YAIR browser integration package at this revision.
repositories.disposition: Useful independent authoring shape for long authored dialogue and explicit host commands; do not adopt as runtime or compiler dependency for current short native scenes.

repositories.title: YarnBound third-party browser runtime

source.cache_limit: Pinned shallow default-head objects and selected blobs; not complete history or all branches.

repositories.observed: This third-party wrapper over a specific bondage.js fork accepts Yarn text, optional variable storage/functions and a command handler, then yields text, options and command results (README; src/yarn-bound.js 1-43, 130-164). Its lookahead toggles runner lookahead while it advances to infer end-of-dialogue and combine text/options; its comments say command sequences can be handled during that lookahead and that one conditional edge case causes commands to be handled prematurely (src/yarn-bound.js 56-127). README says Yarn function callbacks should have no side effects because evaluation may occur unexpectedly. README also explicitly records missing/supplemental Yarn features. YarnBound therefore offers a narrow browser cursor, with behavior bounded by its wrapper and dependency, not a supported official Yarn runtime.
repositories.notice_and_purpose: package.json says ISC, but the repository LICENSE seed is unavailable at the pinned default head. It depends on @mnbroatch/bondage 4.2.4, whose separate license and notices must be examined before bundling. YarnBound is not Yarn Spinner's official Unity package. No copy or dependency adoption is proposed.
repositories.disposition: Review its command/text/options boundary as an adapter design reference only. The README lookahead warning is a dialogue-end detection limitation around commands/set variables; it does not support a speculative side-effect claim.

source.cache_limit: Pinned shallow default-head objects and selected blobs; not complete history or all branches.

evidence.lines: prior exact serialization API locators; file inspected at current revision

repositories.observed: Current pin remains package version 2.4.0. The diff from prior reviewed commit changes package manifests/lock only; current API was still read back. Story.currentChoices filters invisible defaults and renumbers the exposed choices (Story.ts 57-70), so a UI index is not a durable command identity. External binding distinguishes lookahead-safe calls and suppresses or errors for unsafe calls during lookahead/string generation (1837-1872); callbacks must be pure snapshot reads, while game changes stay in a later canonical command. StoryState exposes save/load JSON and declares save format 10/minimum 8 (StoryState.ts 27-50); Flow serialization retains call stack, output, choices and choice threads (Flow.ts 9-87). The compatibility table ends at inklecat 1.2.0 / inkjs 2.3.0, while source reports current story JSON 21/minimum 18; that is not an explicit 2.4.0 compiler/runtime semantic compatibility claim (README 208-229).
repositories.notice_and_purpose: MIT, with inkle Ltd. and inkjs contributor notices; AUTHORS attribution is part of the prior qualified notice evidence. package exports engine-only root and compiler-bearing /full entry (package.json 19-29). No dependency is present or selected in YAIR.
repositories.disposition: Refresh required prior claims to this exact manifest pin; no source behavior delta found in reviewed API paths. No adoption: only a long authored scene could justify optional inkjs, compiler/content pinning and a cursor bridge.

findings.title: Keep narrative choices behind one canonical native command boundary

source_evidence.symbols: specific action-processing rulebook; check, carry out, after and report stage rules

findings.observed_upstream_vs_inference: Observed: Yarn host commands and dialogue/options are separate outputs; YarnBound's lookahead affects its dialogue-end detection around command/set-variable boundaries and includes a documented premature-command edge case; Inform separates action stages. Inference: YAIR can borrow these authoring boundaries without importing any runtime, provided a narrative choice resolves to a typed current native command and no dialogue callback mutates game state.
findings.original_yair_example: Proposal: a scene called Silt Lantern offers three authored responses: reveal a clue only if the player already has attributed trail-reading knowledge; ask its keeper to teach; or leave. Selection resolves to one stable scene action ID, then the native command rechecks present actor, knowledge, consent, costs and current situation. The authored text cannot directly grant a source, knowledge or reward.
findings.current_matching_owner_and_missing_consu: src/scene_definitions.js compileSituation validates stable phase IDs, finite delays, expiry and typed effects (4-20); src/simulation_contracts.js owns commands/effect validation; src/simulation_effects.js projects actual facts, body, knowledge, stock, clock and applies effects; src/gameplay_publication.js stages native snapshots before publishing (docs/ENGINE_AUTHORING.md#skills-and-discovery-native-bindings). Missing: a separate prose-oriented long-scene authoring/cursor layer with stable action identity and native UI. Existing phase/response definitions and registry already cover short caused scenes.
findings.overlap_novelty_route: High overlap for simple branching, conditions, effects and publication; the only distinct value is authoring ergonomics for long prose. Prefer native scene definitions now. If selected later, adapt the boundary independently first; a cursor library may be optional but is not needed for this fixed case.
findings.dependencies_effort_confidence: Required dependencies: none. Optional only if a measured authoring need selects Yarn/Ink. Low effort to author native scene actions; medium/high to add a narrative runner, tooling, cursor save compatibility and accessible UI. Source trace high; missing-consumer assessment medium due to dirty checkout and source-only review.
findings.state_rng_time_stock_publication_save: Resolve UI indexes to stable content/action revision each time. Dialogue conditions read a frozen actor-scoped snapshot; only native command preview/commit may use saved RNG or alter time, exact owned/reserved stock, knowledge, causes and publication. Save cursor plus content identity only if a selected runtime requires it; define migration/old-reader behavior before persistence changes and verify save/reload then.
findings.provenance_license_assets: Yarn Spinner MIT with notices; YarnBound package declares ISC but its pinned LICENSE file is absent and bondage dependency has a separate notice obligation; Inform licensing is per-file/extension under its Artistic License 2.0 route. No code, prose, tags, characters, scene names or assets copied; original Silt Lantern example.
findings.maintenance_removal: Keep authored native scene actions usable if the optional runner is removed. A cursor can be retired only through an explicit safe checkpoint mapping while preserving canonical receipts and consequences; never re-run a paid command from stale dialogue state.
findings.recommendation: Do not select a dialogue dependency for first milestone. If director later selects several long prose scenes, prototype an adapter with a pinned story hash and one real paid/unpaid native response before broad authoring.

findings.title: An optional Ink cursor needs a durable identity and explicit compatibility gate
findings.revision_evidence: Ink 35c63e52f1d36060930dc7ed3cfba38ea224b528; inkjs current pin 6b1153410ab1c4bcfd9ef04eb2f0107f36be7778; prior inkjs source review was edccead8700e9f21be9825d87d8645d8c82a9936.

source_evidence.symbols: save state version and JSON load

findings.observed_upstream_vs_inference: Observed: Inkjs exposes choices as a filtered and reindexed array, persists flow/callstack/output/choice-thread state, and supports only declared save-version bounds; current 2.4.0 isn't listed in the README compatibility table. Inference: a saved index or knot name alone cannot safely resume a paid game-bearing interaction after content changes. Current upstream branch diff from prior pin touched only package manifests/lock, but relevant current APIs and compatibility limits were checked anew.
findings.original_yair_example: Proposal: a multi-visit Glasshouse negotiation may offer a prose branch based on what Joss actually taught the player. A cursor choice identifies a stable authored response, while the native transaction checks the current visit, recipient, knowledge and coin before recording one cause. Restarting stale prose cannot replay the coin or notice effect.
findings.current_matching_owner_and_missing_consu: src/scene_definitions.js and registered simulation situations already own phase/response, cause and expiry; src/simulation_effects.js owns knowledge, exact stock and effects; src/world_instances.js owns realm visit records; native UI is rooted in current domain panels. Missing is only an optional long-form narrative cursor/compiler/content pipeline and its adapter. No general dialogue runtime is needed for current scenes.
findings.overlap_novelty_route: Strong overlap for conditions, short choices, state changes and timing. Distinct value limited to authoring/continuation of long prose. Independently authored static native scenes remain preferred; selective inkjs runtime reuse is a later optional route, not a whole simulation replacement.
findings.dependencies_effort_confidence: Required dependencies: none. Optional: pinned inkjs engine runtime and an author-time Ink compiler; exact compiler/runtime pair and browser/runtime/content sizes remain unmeasured. Medium/high effort for wrapper, stable action mapping, content hash/pin, compiler diagnostics, UI, migration and archive policy. Source facts high confidence; benefit/effort estimate medium.
findings.state_rng_time_stock_publication_save: Compiled content revision and complete opaque cursor save must join one YAIR wrapper/content hash and an explicit supported-version check. Route randomness/rewards only through saved YAIR RNG/receipts, not Ink RNG. Native command owns current clock boundary, actual stock/reservations, player-known facts and atomic publication. Preserve prior paid effects if content/cursor cannot load; reject or map to explicit safe checkpoint rather than replaying. Any persistence addition needs explicit compatibility decision and later browser/save/reload/failure acceptance.
findings.provenance_license_assets: Ink and inkjs MIT, preserve both notices and inkjs AUTHORS attribution. Review file-level licenses for toolchain and assets before any later distribution. No compiler output, library, stories, prose corpus, characters or assets copied in this review.
findings.maintenance_removal: Feature-gate new scene enrollment; retain pinned compiled content for active cursors or migrate each to an authored canonical checkpoint retaining paid receipts. Remove runtime/content only after no supported cursor depends on it; fallback is existing native phase/response definitions.
findings.recommendation: Defer. Current scene definitions are sufficient for first realm and one prestige. Reconsider only after a director-selected long scene demonstrates material authoring benefit over native phases.

findings.title: Grid query libraries do not replace the current directed road graph
findings.observed_upstream_vs_inference: Observed: rot-js A* is coordinate/grid-based with unit edge cost and FOV queries cells/occlusion. TextWorld maker builds generated object/room/proposition worlds and checks generator constraints. TextWorldExpress runs seeded, bounded benchmark episodes with valid action lists and scores. Inference: these tools do not compute YAIR's current authored directed road graph with per-edge played minutes or answer whether a scene command is currently legal; benchmark reset/scoring semantics conflict with continuing durable campaigns.
findings.original_yair_example: The existing proposed courier trip Village to Shack has an authored three-minute edge each direction. Current route preparation is an optional timed action; carrying a parcel or reaching a meeting is checked by native route/actor state. Grid A* cannot infer road time or cause a paid travel command, and a benchmark shortest path cannot record the courier's accepted work or remembered return.
findings.current_matching_owner_and_missing_consu: src/frontier_campaign.js currently authors Village/Shack routes with minutes; src/realm_connections.js and world_instances.js handle authored realm/physical connection semantics; src/scene_definitions.js registers causal situations; src/simulation_contracts.js/effects and gameplay_publication own legal effects and durable commit. Missing only if a future selected world introduces spatial grid geometry: a grid query adapter mapping cells to existing typed movement/observation commands. No current road-graph consumer is missing because the current routes are already represented as explicit graph edges.
findings.overlap_novelty_route: Current route/path modeling fully overlaps the intended near-term use. rot-js adds distinct A*/FOV only for a real grid. TextWorld may inform offline authoring constraints; Express is an independent benchmark harness. Adapt no implementation/dependency now.
findings.dependencies_effort_confidence: No required dependency. rot-js BSD-3-Clause if later adopted, TextWorld MIT and TextWorldExpress Apache-2.0. Current no-fit confidence high for the different topology/benchmark purposes; effort estimate not needed. Any future grid adapter is medium effort because a pure spatial result still needs native legal movement and save/time semantics.
findings.state_rng_time_stock_publication_save: For current roads, stable graph IDs and authored durations remain content; travel consumes the current native clock/command and only updates location at committed boundary. Grid geometry would require a separate seed/realized-map policy and saved positions; query preview must not draw RNG or publish exploration. TextWorld benchmark reset/episode RNG and TextWorldExpress step scores must never become YAIR campaign save, clock, inventory or reward policy.
findings.provenance_license_assets: Preserve rot BSD-3-Clause, TextWorld MIT and TextWorldExpress Apache-2.0 notices if future code reuse is separately selected. No graph library, benchmark simulator, authored scenarios, benchmark prose/data or assets copied. Upstream asset/content rights were not inferred from repository code license.
findings.maintenance_removal: Current authored graph has no library lifecycle. If a future grid module is removed, preserve app-owned geometry and canonical movement/observation receipts while replacing pure path/FOV queries. Benchmark-only experiments can be discarded without save migration if isolated from game state.
findings.recommendation: Do not add spatial or benchmark dependencies for current road graph and scene commands. Keep TextWorld/TextWorldExpress as explicitly non-runtime research comparators.
